meta.notes: Compiled via web search/fetch. Web-search budget was exhausted part-way through Part 3; items marked 'unverified' come from prior knowledge and must be checked. Figures are as reported by the cited source; nothing has been estimated unless labelled 'derived'.

founded.value: 2012, Sydney; founders Lachlan McKnight (CEO), Evan Tait-Styles (CTO), Ursula Hogben. Started as online legal-document service, incorporated legal practice 2014, membership model adopted 2019

model.value: Subscription ('membership') law firm: unlimited business-as-usual legal work (consults, drafting, reviews, trade marks, employment/HR) for a fixed weekly fee billed monthly; litigation, corporate transactions/M&A/fundraising charged hourly (50% discount for 3- and 5-year members). Min 12-month term; discounts for 3/5-year terms; 30-day money-back for new members. Revenue mix (Feb 2022): ~50% subscription, ~25% hourly, ~25% fixed fee (legacy).

pricing_uk_gbp.value: LV Pro: £115 to £620+ per week + VAT, by business size/contract length (website, Oct 2026). Legal Futures Mar-2025: £115-£399/week; at 2022 launch £49-£329/week. LV Essentials (<2 employees) price not published. Desk Extension (in-house) and H&S add-on unpriced.

pricing_au_aud.value: LV Pro: A$219 to A$1,350+ per week ex GST by business size; LV Essentials: A$119-A$149/week (website, Oct 2026). Earlier (2019) subscription launched at A$149/month.

pricing_nz_nzd.value: At Jan-2021 NZ launch: 'LVConnect' membership NZ$199 + GST per month. Current NZ tier pricing not retrieved (site fetch blocked).

revenue.value: Capital Brief (1 Oct 2024): ~A$50m 'this year' for AU+NZ and A$13m UK; target A$100m by 2027. Rally Legal (Feb 2022): ~A$25m annualised cited as scale needed. SmartCompany Smart50 2017: A$7.8m revenue, 341% growth. Company does not publish turnover (CEO declined, Mar 2025).

uk_launch.value: UK expansion announced Nov 2021 (CEO relocating); UK entity incorporated 26 Oct 2021; began trading from Manchester 2022 (ABS licence May 2022; Legal Futures June 2022: 7 staff, ~100 new members/month group-wide, 85% renewal, NPS 70). Lawyers Weekly: entered UK Nov 2021, NZ Oct 2020 (went live Jan 2021).

uk_leadership.value: No UK MD named in press. CEO Lachlan McKnight (based Sydney, relocated to UK for a period 2022). Group: Evan Tait-Styles CTO, Chris Bambury CFO, Mark McMinn CRO, Lauren Wray Head of Growth. UK: Anthony Satti Co-Head of Legal / Corporate & Commercial Practice Leader (Pro-Manchester, Nov 2025).

headcount.value: Mar 2025: UK ~40 staff (28 lawyers, 12 sales), mostly Manchester, ~10 remote, target 100; Australia 200+ (also provides UK back office). Feb 2022: 130-138 staff group. 2017: ~65. Companies House avg UK employees FY25: 41.

members_clients.value: >4,500 active clients group-wide (Quadrant, Mar 2025); ~40% of new business from UK (Mar 2025). 2022: ~100 new members/month, 85% renewal, NPS 70. Site claims 110,000+ businesses assisted historically.

growth_rate.value: '30%+ p.a.' (Quadrant, Mar 2025); 40% YoY (Nov 2021); 30%+ YoY in Australia (Feb 2022); 341% (2017).

funding_ownership.value: Not bootstrapped at present: founder-owned (McKnight Family Trust ultimate controller through FY2024) until Quadrant Private Equity acquired a stake announced 11-12 Mar 2025 (undisclosed terms; first deal from A$660m Quadrant Growth Fund No.3, which targets A$50-100m per company). UK filings show ultimate parent became QPE Epsilon 1 Pty Ltd and Quadrant's Elkhouri/Darville became PSCs from 9 May 2025, consistent with Quadrant control. Capital Brief (Oct 2024) described Gilbert + Tobin as 'only external institutional investor' pre-Quadrant (G+T also advised on the sale). Sell-side advisers Allier Capital, G+T; buy-side PwC, OC&C, Corrs.

awards.value: FT Innovative Lawyers 2026 shortlists (Innovative Business Models; Strategic Direction); LexisNexis Legal Awards 2026 finalist/highly commended; The Lawyer Awards 2024/2025/2026 finalist; Law Firm of the Year, Australasian Law Awards 2021 & 2022; FT1000 fastest-growing law firm APAC 2018 & 2021; Australasian Lawyer Fast Firms 2023, 2024; AFR Fast 100 finalist 2018, 2020; Smart50 #9 (2017); Innovator of the Year, Australian Law Awards 2016; Business Awards UK Commercial Law Firm of the Year 2024.

sprintlaw.value: Sydney online fixed-fee/subscription firm (founders Alex Solo, Tomoyuki Hachigo). £1.2m first equity raise Dec 2019 (revenue +250% in 2019; 7,000+ clients). Launched UK (England & Wales) 8 June 2021 funded by ~A$1m angel round (incl. ex-Smartgroup CEO Deven Billimoria); UK MD Adil Khan (ex-Lexoo). Membership launched 2020 at £399/yr; 3,000+ members across UK/AU/NZ as at 2024. AFR Fast Starters 2021. Revenue not disclosed.

market.metric: LSB Small Business Legal Needs Survey (wave 4, YouGov fieldwork Jul-Sep 2021, published Apr 2022): incidence
market.value: 32% experience a legal issue annually (=1.8m businesses, 15.4m issues); trading 21%, regulation 9%, employees 8%, tax 7%; 24% of 1-employee firms vs 48% of 2-9 and 44%+ of 10-49

market.metric: LSB SBLNS: response to legal issue
market.value: 25% used professional help as main adviser (28% in 2017); 44-46% sought to resolve entirely alone (53% in 2013); 8% took no action (10% in 2017); 19% asked independent adviser; main advisers: accountants 22%, solicitors 16%, not-for-profit 10%; only 10% view lawyers as cost-effective; 4% used legal expenses insurance; 48% paid for service; fixed price most common pricing (44%); 70% satisfied

market.metric: LSB SBLNS: unmet need (OECD experimental model)
market.value: Of those with an issue, ~12% had an unmet legal need vs 3% met (LSB news/Legal Futures); 'vast majority' of needs requiring professional support are not met; 1-9 employee firms least likely to use professional help
71% of small businesses did not use the internet for any listed legal task; 54% of legal services delivered by email, 43% phone, 16% in person, 15% video
market.source: LSB Small Business Legal Needs wave 4 PDF

market.value: 66% of adults had a legal issue in last 4 years; 52% of those got professional help, 38% no help, 11% non-professional only; unmet need 32% (31% in 2019; corrected from 36%); ~9 in 10 satisfied with adviser
